question.name: Scope
question.answer: Premium design theme management for kindly-web UI. Store purple spectrum (10 shades), gold spectrum (5 shades), glass tints (3 variants), and theme mode (light/dark/auto) in lockfree cache-aligned capsule.
question.rationale: Replaces mutable theme state with atomic capsule for zero-lock UI theming

question.name: Assumptions
question.answer: ASSUME: Color values are compile-time constants (never change at runtime) ASSUME: Relaxed memory ordering sufficient for independent UI state ASSUME: Theme mode toggles are infrequent (human-speed, not high-frequency) VERIFY: All assumptions validated with property tests

question.name: Constraints
question.answer: - WASM target (no mmap, no threads, limited SIMD) - Cache alignment critical (64B minimum, 128B chosen for warm tier) - Color packing required (fit 18 colors in 128B) - Zero dependencies beyond atomic_capsule

question.name: Context
question.answer: Premium web UI with glassmorphism effects. Theme must support real-time mode switching, multiple color scales for gradients, and glass tint variants without locking.

question.name: Success
question.answer: - Color lookup: <5ns (relaxed reads) - Mode toggle: <20ns (CAS operation) - Zero race conditions - 100% compile-time verification - Cache-aligned (128B)

question.name: Failure
question.answer: - Cache misses from unaligned access - Race conditions from non-atomic reads - Memory bloat from inefficient packing - WASM incompatibility from platform-specific features

question.name: Patterns
question.answer: - Atomic Capsule Pattern (T1): Lockfree coordination for UI state - Bit Packing: 2 colors per AtomicU64 (32-bit RGBA each) - SWeMR: Single-writer (theme setter), many-readers (UI components)

question.name: Alternatives
question.answer: Rejected: Mutex<ThemeState> (locking overhead, 32ns vs 5ns) Rejected: RwLock (still locks readers) Rejected: DashMap (overkill for 18 colors, 100ns overhead) Chosen: Atomic capsule with bit packing (proven 3.3× speedup)

question.name: Trade-offs
question.answer: Optimizing for: Read latency (5ns), zero locks, cache alignment Trading off: Slight write complexity (packing/unpacking) Justification: Reads 1000× more frequent than writes in UI

question.name: Computational Capsule
question.answer: Tier 1 Atomic (lockfree coordination)

tier-selection.rationale: Theme state is coordination primitive: multiple UI components read colors, single setter updates mode. T1 atomic provides lockfree SWeMR pattern.
tier-selection.speedup: 3-10× vs mutex-based theme state (proven in circuit breaker)

question.name: Rust Transform
question.answer: - Rust atomics: AtomicU64, AtomicU32 with Ordering::Relaxed (independent UI state) - #[repr(C, align(128))]: Cache alignment for warm tier - const fn: Compile-time capsule initialization - Bit packing: Manual pack_two_colors/unpack_two_colors for RGBA storage

question.name: Scope
question.answer: Premium glassmorphism effect engine with SIMD-accelerated 4-layer blur calculation. Store blur levels (sm/md/lg/xl: 8/16/24/32px), saturation (Q16.16 fixed-point), and 4 opacity layers in SIMD-aligned capsule.
question.rationale: Replaces scalar blur calculations with f32x4 SIMD for 2-4× speedup in glass effect rendering

question.name: Assumptions
question.answer: ASSUME: portable_simd feature available (nightly Rust) ASSUME: f32x4 SIMD operations supported on target (x86_64 SSE, aarch64 NEON, WASM simd128) ASSUME: Blur calculations are independent (can be vectorized) VERIFY: SIMD and scalar implementations match (property tests)

question.name: Constraints
question.answer: - WASM target (requires +simd128 target feature, not all runtimes support) - Nightly Rust required (portable_simd unstable) - SIMD alignment critical (128B for f32x4 operations) - Fallback to scalar for non-SIMD platforms

question.name: Context
question.answer: Premium web UI glassmorphism effects. Need real-time blur/saturation/opacity adjustments for multi-layer glass surfaces without frame drops.

question.name: Success
question.answer: - 4-layer blur calculation: <50ns (SIMD vectorization) - Single blur level read: <10ns - SIMD vs scalar equivalence: 100% accuracy - 2-4× speedup vs scalar baseline

question.name: Failure
question.answer: - SIMD misalignment (cache miss penalty) - SIMD precision loss (f32 rounding errors) - Platform incompatibility (WASM without simd128) - Nightly instability (portable_simd breaking changes)

question.name: Patterns
question.answer: - SIMD Capsule Pattern (T2): Vectorized computation for data parallelism - Fixed-Point Saturation (Q16.16): Deterministic precision for saturation value - Bit Packing: 2 f32 values per AtomicU64 (raw bits storage)

question.name: Alternatives
question.answer: Rejected: Scalar f32 calculations (4× slower, 100-200ns) Rejected: Pre-computed blur tables (memory overhead, inflexible) Rejected: GPU shaders (overkill for UI, latency overhead) Chosen: SIMD f32x4 (2-4× speedup, proven in Hebbian learning)

question.name: Trade-offs
question.answer: Optimizing for: Blur calculation throughput (4 layers in <50ns) Trading off: Nightly Rust requirement, platform compatibility Justification: 2-4× speedup critical for 60fps UI rendering

question.name: Computational Capsule
question.answer: Tier 2 SIMD (vectorized computation)

tier-selection.rationale: 4-layer blur calculation is data-parallel: same operation on 4 independent blur levels. T2 SIMD provides f32x4 vectorization for 2-19× speedup.
